questions.q: Which Azure CLI command actually deploys Overlook's Bicep template into a resource group?
options: az bicep deploy
az deployment group create
az sql server create
terraform apply
questions.explain: az deployment group create takes --template-file and --parameters and deploys the Bicep template into the named resource group.

questions.q: How should sqlAdminPassword's actual value be supplied on the deploy command line?
options: Typed directly as plain text after --parameters
Hardcoded into the Bicep file as a default
From an environment variable (or CI/CD secret store) set immediately before the command runs, never typed in plain text or committed to source control
Emailed to the DBA beforehand
questions.explain: An environment variable keeps the real password out of shell history and out of any script file checked into source control.

questions.q: What actually changes between the dev deployment command and the prod deployment command in this lesson?
options: The entire Bicep template must be rewritten
The resource group, resource names, and which secret variable holds the password — the template and its resource definitions stay unchanged
The sku block must be edited by hand for prod
Nothing changes; the exact same command deploys both
questions.explain: This is Lesson 5's parameterization paying off — only the --parameters values differ, not the template itself.

questions.q: What are the two independent ways this lesson confirms a deployment actually succeeded?
options: Asking a colleague, and checking email
The CLI's own exit code/output (provisioningState: Succeeded), and the Azure Portal's separate deployment history for the resource group
Running the deployment twice and comparing results
Checking the database's row count
questions.explain: Checking two independent systems — the CLI and the Portal's own history — is safer than trusting a single source of truth.

questions.q: What does Overlook's environment still lack immediately after this lesson's deployment?
options: A server and a database
Any firewall rule allowing a specific client to connect, auditing, and a failover group — those come in Chapters 3 and 4
Any form of IaC
A resource group
questions.explain: This lesson deploys the base server/database; connectivity rules, deeper security, and HA/DR are deliberately built on top of it in later chapters.
